page: Amazon Web Services c7i.48xlarge is a compute-optimized instance built on the AWS Nitro hypervisor architecture. It features dual-socket 4th Generation Intel Xeon Scalable (8488C) processors running at 3.2 GHz, providing 192 dedicated virtual CPUs across 96 physical cores with simultaneous multithreading enabled. The instance integrates 384 GB of 5 GHz DDR5 system memory, maintaining a classic compute-oriented memory-to-vCPU ratio of 2 GB per thread. There is no bundled local storage or dedicated discrete GPU hardware, relying entirely on network-attached storage while offering a 50 Gbps baseline network bandwidth interface.

Performance benchmarks reflect high compute density and throughput. The platform demonstrates top-tier multi-core performance, achieving 169,731.29 in stress-ng multi-core tests and 123,408.48 in PassMark CPU evaluations. Supported by Intel AMX and AVX-512 vector extensions, it excels in accelerated cryptography, ray tracing, and CPU-based vector matrix tasks, including prompt processing across small to large language models. Memory throughput is substantial, registering 419.18 GB/sec in uncached read bandwidth, which aids static web serving throughput exceeding 115 GB/sec and Redis key-value operations reaching 176.17 million operations per second.

From an architectural standpoint, the instance trades local disk access for consolidated multi-socket compute density and high-bandwidth network connectivity. In terms of cost efficiency relative to compute capacity, it maximizes throughput per allocated core for parallel batch jobs rather than persistent local disk manipulation. The server is well suited for compute-intensive workloads such as continuous integration build pipelines, large-scale distributed caching, financial simulations, static web serving clusters, and CPU-based machine learning inference.
description: Amazon Web Services c7i.48xlarge is a compute-optimized Nitro-based cloud instance powered by 4th Generation Intel Xeon 8488C processors. Featuring 192 dedicated vCPUs across 96 physical cores operating at 3.2 GHz, it is paired with 384 GB of DDR5 memory at 5 GHz, delivering 2 GB of RAM per vCPU. The instance omits local ephemeral storage and GPU acceleration, providing 50 Gbps of baseline network bandwidth to interface with network storage and external infrastructure. Benchmark results place it in the top tier for multi-core compute throughput, extended instruction operations, uncached memory reads, static web throughput, and in-memory key-value processing. Hardware support for AVX-512 and AMX extensions enables accelerated vector operations and CPU-based LLM inference. This profile is engineered for parallel compute tasks, CI/CD compilation workloads, distributed in-memory databases, and high-throughput network applications.
